```{r}
#| label: Libraries setup
#| results: hide

#Load Libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(ggplot2)
library(kableExtra)
```

<H3>Part 1: Raw Data Structure</H3>

Below is an example table showing my raw understory data structure:

- Plot ID: Unique ID. "UB" for unburned control plots, "BBB" for burn plots not receiving augmentation, and BBN for burn plots receiving augmentation.

- Times Burned: Number of times area burned in recorded times. 1x burn for plots burnt only in 2000. 2x for plots burnt both in 2000 and 1977. 0x for control plots.

- Augmentation: Whether area received post-fire augmentation (true/false condition)

- Species Code: Unique taxon code for each recorded species/bare substrate

- Veg Type: Taxon code classified according to vegetation type (Native woody, invasive woody, invasive grass, etc.). No repeats only logs first occurrence of a species type at a point, so for example if both StyTam and DodVis (both native woody) were recorded at point, only one is logged. This makes classifying plots by veg cover type easier. Veg Type with repeats logs all vegetation recorded by type.

```{r}
#| label: example dataframe
#| out-width: "75%"
#| tbl-cap: Table 1


#load in my data
UnderstoryData_Raw <- read.csv(here("Data","RawData","UnderstoryData_Raw.csv"))

UnderstoryData_Raw_Sample_Table <- UnderstoryData_Raw |>
  #only 20 rows as example
  head(20)|>
  kbl(caption="Example Plot Data Structure",
      col.names = c("Plot ID", "Times Burned", "Augmentation","Point ID","Species Code","Veg Type (No Repeats)","Veg Type (Repeats"),
      align = "lcccccc")|>
  kable_styling(full_width=FALSE)|>
  row_spec(0,bold=TRUE)|>
  kable_classic()

UnderstoryData_Raw_Sample_Table
```

<h3>Part 2: Converting raw data to cumulative tally</h3>

Raw understory files can be fed into a function called "Species Matrix" which tallies the number of times a taxon code was logged on a per-plot basis, then renders a wide-format table with all the tallies.

```{r}
#| label: example-dataframe-tally
#| out-width: "75%"
#| tbl-cap: Table 2
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| results: asis

#function instructions
Species_Matrix <-function(data,
                          output = here("Data","WideData","UnderstoryCover_Tally.csv"),
                          plot_col = "Plot_ID",
                          taxon_col = "Taxon_Code"){
  #columns as symbols
  plot_col <- ensym(plot_col)
  taxon_col <- ensym(taxon_col)
  
  #summary generation
  summary_matrix <- data|>
    #filter any missing records
    filter(!is.na(!!taxon_col))|>
    #group by plot and taxon code, then tally
    group_by(!!plot_col,!!taxon_col)|>
    summarise(tally = n(),.groups = "drop")|>
    #pivot data wide
    pivot_wider(names_from = !!taxon_col,
                values_from = tally)
  
  #export dataframe as csv
  write_csv(summary_matrix, output)
  
  message("Species tally matrix successfully saved to: ", output)
  return(summary_matrix)
}

#running the function
UnderstoryCover_Tally <- Species_Matrix(data = UnderstoryData_Raw)

#example of dataframe rendered by function
UnderstoryCover_Tally[, 1:10] |>
  #only 10 rows as example
  head(10)|>
  kbl(caption="Example Understory Plot Tally",
      col.names = c("Plot ID", "AndGlo", "AndVir","AruBam","BareSoil","DodVis","HypRad","MetPol","MorGah","PteAqu"),
      align = "lccccccccc")|>
  kable_styling(full_width=FALSE)|>
  row_spec(0,bold=TRUE)|>
  kable_classic()
```

I then edited the output document in Google Sheets to re-add columns for "Times Burned" and "Augment". I save the output as "UnderstoryCover_Tally_Edited.csv" in my wide data format. At this point I want to compare species cover from this data to the 2010 data. This will require me to standardize by converting all raw tallies to percentages (since I read 93 points per plot and the 2010 study read 100 points per plot).

```{r}
#| label: Converting tally data for graphing
#| results: hide

#read csv
UnderstoryCover_Tally_Edited <- read_csv(here("Data","WideData","UnderstoryCover_Tally_Edited.csv"))
UnderstoryCover_Tally_Edited$Times_Burned <- as.factor(UnderstoryCover_Tally_Edited$Times_Burned)
head(UnderstoryCover_Tally_Edited)

#take edited tally, divide by 93, then
UnderstoryCover_Tally_Edited <- UnderstoryCover_Tally_Edited|>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ .x / 93),
         #add year for new data
         Year = factor("2026"))|> 
  relocate(Year, .after = 1)

```

I then need to convert the old 2010 data to a format where I can compare the two years. The 2010 data has plots as columns and species as rows, so I will flip them with the transpose tool.

```{r}
#| label: 2010 understory data manipulation
#| results: hide

UnderstoryCover_Tally_2010_Raw <- read_csv(here("Data","WideData","UnderstoryCover_Tally_2010_Raw.csv"))

head(UnderstoryCover_Tally_2010_Raw)
#switch rows and columns
UnderstoryCover_Tally_2010 <- UnderstoryCover_Tally_2010_Raw |>
  t() |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "Original Headers", .name_repair = "minimal")

#output is cleaned in sheets and re-imported as "UnderstoryCover_Tally_2010_Edited.csv"
UnderstoryCover_Tally_2010_Edited <- read_csv(here("Data","WideData","UnderstoryCover_Tally_2010_Edited.csv"))
#convert factors
UnderstoryCover_Tally_2010_Edited$Times_Burned <- as.factor(UnderstoryCover_Tally_2010_Edited$Times_Burned)
UnderstoryCover_Tally_2010_Edited$Augment <- as.factor(UnderstoryCover_Tally_2010_Edited$Augment)
#data check
head(UnderstoryCover_Tally_2010_Edited)

UnderstoryCover_Tally_2010_Edited <- UnderstoryCover_Tally_2010_Edited|>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ .x / 100),
         Year = factor("2010"))|> 
  relocate(Year, .after = 1)
```

With both data frames converted to the same wide format, they just need to be pivoted to long format and stitched together so they can be compared in a graph. For this comparison I chose only species that appeared in at least five plots per survey year.

```{r}
#| label: combined understory cover data
#| results: hide

#pivot 2026 tally to long data format
UnderstoryCover_Tally_Long_Edited <- UnderstoryCover_Tally_Edited|>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = AndGlo:FesRub,
    names_to = "Species",
    values_to = "Abundance")|>
  #filter out NA
  filter(!is.na(Abundance))|>
  group_by(Species)|>
  #calculate how many plots a species appears in
  mutate(n_plots = n_distinct(Plot_ID))|>
  #keeping just species in at least five plots
  filter(n_plots >= 5)

#output data file
write_csv(UnderstoryCover_Tally_Long_Edited,file = here("Data","LongData","UnderstoryCover_Tally_Long_Edited.csv"))

#pivot 2010 tally to long data format
Understory_Tally_Long_Edited_2010 <- UnderstoryCover_Tally_2010_Edited|>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = AcaKoa:Log,
    names_to = "Species",
    values_to = "Abundance")|>
  #filter out NA
  filter(!is.na(Abundance))|>
  group_by(Species)|>
  #calculate how many plots a species appears in
  mutate(n_plots = n_distinct(Plot_ID))|>
  filter(n_plots >= 5)

#output data file
write_csv(Understory_Tally_Long_Edited_2010,file = here("Data","LongData","UnderstoryCover_Tally_Long_2010_Edited.csv"))

Understory_Tally_Long_Combined <- bind_rows(Understory_Tally_Long_Edited_2010,UnderstoryCover_Tally_Long_Edited)
Understory_Tally_Long_Combined

#output data file
write_csv(Understory_Tally_Long_Combined,file = here("Data","LongData","UnderstoryCover_Tally_Long_Combined.csv"))


```

<h3>Part 3: Boxplot Comparisons of Species Cover Across Years</h3>

Now they can be graphed to see if there are trends with species cover in different augmentation and burn number factors.

```{r}
#| label: Understory box plots by species cover
#| fig-height: 10
#| fig-width: 10
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| results: hide

#boxplots comparing 2010 and 2026
ggplot(Understory_Tally_Long_Combined,
       aes(x = Augment,
           y = Abundance,
           fill = Year)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.shape = 16) +
  facet_wrap(~ Species, scales = "free_y",axes = "all") +
  labs(
    title = "Change from 2010-2026 in Percent Cover",
    subtitle = "Species found in at least 5 plots",
    x = "Augmentation",
    y = "Abundance in Plot"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

```

Some quick observations:

- StyTam cover rose across all classes in all years

- DodVis cover higher in plots that were augmented for both 2010 and 2026, but especially the latter

- Leaf Litter much higher in 2010 observations, but I suspect this is due to sampler more than changes to ground cover

- Augmented plots had much more AcaKoa than not augmented plots in 2010. Now they do not.

<h3>Part 4: Comparing Cumulative Cover Types Across Years</h3>

Most cover stats from the 2010 report condense species cover to three main categories (Exotic, Native, No Veg). In order to compare the two, I will condense my 2026 data so it can compiled in one large dataset. Then I can compare the years 2010 and 2016 across these three main cover metrics.

```{r}
#| label: Understory box plots by cover type
#| fig-height: 10
#| fig-width: 10
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| results: hide

#group existing veg types in raw data into even more simplified groups for comparison
Understory_Data_byCoverType <- UnderstoryData_Raw %>%
  group_by(Plot_ID, Point_ID) %>%
  mutate(
    temp_cat = case_when(
      Veg_Type_Repeats %in% c("Native_Woody", "Native_Herbaceous", "Native_Grass") ~ "Native",
      Veg_Type_Repeats %in% c("Invasive_Woody", "Invasive_Herbaceous", "Invasive_Grass") ~ "Exotic",
      Veg_Type_Repeats == "Bare_Substrate" ~ "No veg",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    # Check for duplicates of the exact veg type
    New_Status = if_else(
      !is.na(temp_cat) & !duplicated(Veg_Type_Repeats), 
      temp_cat, 
      NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-temp_cat) %>%
  ungroup()

print(n = 50,Understory_Data_byCoverType)

#convert raw data to percentages
Understory_Plot_Tally_byCoverType <- Species_Matrix(Understory_Data_byCoverType,taxon_col = "New_Status",output = here("Data","WideData","UnderstoryPlot_Tally_byCoverType.csv"))

Understory_Plot_Tally_byCoverType <- Understory_Plot_Tally_byCoverType|>
  #divide by total plot points then multiply by 100 for percentage
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ (.x / 93) * 100))
Understory_Plot_Tally_byCoverType
write_csv(Understory_Plot_Tally_byCoverType,file = here("Data","WideData","UnderstoryPlot_Tally_byCoverType.csv"))

#2026 plot tally combined with 2010 data and re-imported as combined csv
Understory_Plot_Tally_byCoverType_Combined <- read_csv(here("Data","WideData","UnderstoryPlot_Tally_byCoverType_Combined.csv"))

#pivot data long for graphing
Understory_Plot_Tally_byCoverType_Combined_Long <- Understory_Plot_Tally_byCoverType_Combined|>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = Native:`No veg`,
    names_to = "Veg_Type",
    values_to = "Percentages")

#boxplot comparing cover types across years
Understory_Plot_Tally_byCoverType_Combined_Long$Year <- as.factor(Understory_Plot_Tally_byCoverType_Combined_Long$Year)
Understory_Plot_Tally_byCoverType_Combined_Long$Times_Burned <- as.factor(Understory_Plot_Tally_byCoverType_Combined_Long$Times_Burned)

ggplot(Understory_Plot_Tally_byCoverType_Combined_Long,
       aes(x = Augment,
           y = Percentages,
           fill = Year)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.shape = 16) +
  facet_wrap(~ Veg_Type) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 100),
    breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 10))+
  labs(
    title = "Change from 2010-2026",
    subtitle = "Percent Cover",
    x = "Augmentation",
    y = "Abundance in Plot"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

```

Initial thoughts:

- Clear difference between surveyors as far as what was marked "No Veg". Will have to ask Sierra at HVNP for her thoughts on how "No Veg" was documented in past survey.

- Higher range for native cover in augmented plots vs. non-augmented in 2010, and similar trend taking place in 2026. I want to dig into this further.

- Higher recorded exotic cover in control plots in 2026 vs 2010. I wonder if this is actual expansion of invasive cover or if surveyor affects results.
